Latin word

exclūdō

exclūdō, exclūdere, exclūsī, exclūsum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; ab + abl., or the abl. alone · Conjugation on Wiktionary

shut out, keep out, exclude; rule out

In this lexicon

  • exclude

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.134: nec vērō … exclūdat aliōs; Quint. 1.1.26: nōn exclūdō, I don’t rule it out

Examples

  • nec vērō, tamquam in possessiōnem suam vēnerit, exclūdat aliōs, sed cum reliquīs in rēbus, tum in sermōne commūnī vicissitūdinem nōn inīquam putet

    and he should not shut others out, as if he had come into his own property, but think it fair, in conversation as in everything else, to take turnsCic. Off. 1.134

    In the entry for exclude

  • nōn exclūdō autem, id quod est inventum irrītandae ad discendum īnfantiae grātiā, eburneās etiam litterārum fōrmās in lūsum offerre

    I don’t rule out the thing invented to tempt small children to learn, giving them ivory letters to play withQuint. 1.1.26

    In the entry for exclude
